title: PR triage + follow-up checklist (scratchpad)
content:
Notes to self - PR triage and follow-ups

Context: quick scratchpad for PR #4123 (mesh routing + cache-key changes). I started a pass during lunch — these are raw, keep as reminders. Will convert into formal review comments for the PR later.

Quick summary of what I saw:
- PR touches routing layer (router/service_matcher.go), KV cache keys (cache/keys.go), and one small change to the batcher which alters target sequence length heuristics.
- Tests added, but most are unit-level; integration tests for cross-region fallback are missing.
- Perf numbers included in the PR description are promising but only for synthetic microbenchmarks (seq len 64).

Top-level risks / things to verify:
- Cache key change can increase cache misses for some prefixes — regression risk for production traffic patterns. Need a safemode flag or fallback.
- Routing policy change may alter weighted traffic distribution; check metrics after canary.
- Batcher heuristic tweak interacts with existing autoscaler threshold; might increase bursty latency.

Review checklist (will post as comments where relevant):
- [ ] Author: add explicit migration note in PR description if cache key format changed (impact: cached entries become invalid).
- [ ] Add a feature flag / server flag gate for new routing behavior so we can toggle without deploy rollback.
- [ ] Add integration test for cross-region fallback with a simulated capacity outage (linear test harness?).
- [ ] Add a load test sample (artillery/locust script snippet) that reproduces microbenchmark inputs used for perf claim. Attach dataset or config.
- [ ] Ensure KV cache backwards compatibility: document old key format and include a short compatibility shim OR add migration command.
- [ ] Run ruff/flake8 + go vet on changed files; fix linter warnings (I noticed two TODO comments left).
- [ ] Add explicit metrics emitted for cache hit/miss per key-version to ease post-deploy analysis.

Code smells / specific lines to comment on (notes for later):
- router/service_matcher.go: around line 178 new weighting math uses float64 division without stability checks — potential divide-by-zero if weights are zero. Suggest clamp or default weight.
- cache/keys.go: newKeyV2() appends timestamp for entropy; this will change cache granularity and break cold-start hits. Consider adding namespace prefix instead and keep timestamp optional behind flag.
- batcher/heuristics.go: the heuristic now prefers larger batches for seq_len>128; but downstream model memory isn't considered. Add a guard or fallback to prevent OOM on smaller GPU nodes.

Refactor ideas (later follow-up issues):
- Split cache key construction into a small package with versioning helpers (keys/version.go) so future changes are less invasive.
- Introduce a single source-of-truth for routing policies (maybe a proto + YAML) and generate the go structs; reduces divergence between team edits.
- Centralize batcher constraints (cpu/gpu/mem) into a resource-aware estimator used by both autoscaler and batcher. Open a tech-debt ticket for this.

Follow-ups / action items (assign after PR accepted):
- [ ] TD-1: Create migration plan for cache keys (estimate: 2-3 days) — owner: me. Linked to RL-2417.
- [ ] TD-2: Add canary + metric dashboards for routing weights (Grafana) — owner: Maya.
- [ ] TD-3: Add integration test to ci-integration suite to simulate region failover (owner: Liam).
- [ ] TD-4: Add perf harness config and store results in artifacts for PRs touching batcher (owner: me).

Questions to ask the author (to include in review comments):
- Did you consider keeping the cache key version additive (v1 -> v2) rather than replacing? If so, why choose replace?
- Can you share the raw load profile used for microbenchmarks? I want to replay it against staging.
- Is the routing change targeted only at hosted customers or also for Dedicated/Private? Impact surface differs.

Testing notes (what I ran locally quickly):
- unit tests: all pass (go test ./... -short) but I had to re-generate mocks for router_test.go.
- ran a small local load profile with 1000 requests, seq_len 64 and 512: saw a 2-3% higher miss rate with new key on seq 512 (need reproducible harness).
- linter: ruff flagged unused import in batcher/optimizer.py (small Python harness).

Suggested review comment snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- "Can you add a migration note to the PR description outlining how existing cache entries will be handled? If possible, include a short compatibility shim or a migration script."
- "Please gate this routing change behind a feature flag controlled by config; we should be able to toggle routing behavior during canary without redeploying."
- "Add an integration test for region fallback. Right now unit tests look good but we need a higher-level smoke to ensure routing+cache interplay on failover."

Estimate of review effort: 45-60 minutes for full pass + extra 1-3 days of follow-up work if we implement migration and tests.

Random notes / TODOs to self:
- Check if RL-2417 already covers cache migration; if not, open a new ticket.
- Add a short blurb to the release notes about the potential cache invalidation impact.
- Reach out to Solutions Eng if Dedicated customers need advance notice.

End of scratchpad. Will trim and convert into formal review comments before posting.
